headline: Iran threatens to close Strait of Hormuz after new US sanctions package targets oil exports
body: Tehran's naval command issued a statement warning it could disrupt tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz in response to a fresh round of US sanctions announced this week targeting Iranian crude exports and shadow fleet vessels.

headline: Insurance premiums for Gulf tanker transits spike 40% amid rising tensions
body: War-risk insurance premiums for vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz have jumped sharply this week as underwriters price in a higher probability of disruption following the latest US-Iran standoff.

headline: Houthi forces claim new missile strike on commercial vessel in Red Sea
body: A commercial tanker reported damage after a missile strike attributed to Houthi forces near the Bab-el-Mandeb strait, the latest in a series of attacks that have pushed several shipping majors to reroute around the Cape of Good Hope.

headline: US Treasury sanctions additional entities linked to Iranian crude exports
body: The US Treasury's OFAC added several shipping and trading entities to its sanctions list, targeting networks believed to facilitate Iranian crude sales, further tightening pressure on Tehran's oil revenue.

headline: Indian refiners quietly increase Russian ESPO crude purchases as Gulf risk rises
body: Indian refiners including IOCL and Reliance have reportedly increased term discussions for Russian ESPO blend cargoes as a hedge against potential Strait of Hormuz disruption risk.

headline: Saudi Arabia calls for de-escalation, says exports continuing normally for now
body: Saudi officials said crude exports through the Gulf remain unaffected for now, while urging all parties to avoid actions that could threaten freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz.

headline: Suez Canal Authority reports continued drop in transit volumes
body: Transit volumes through the Suez Canal remain well below pre-crisis levels as shipping lines continue to favor the longer Cape of Good Hope route to avoid Red Sea risk.

headline: Cape of Good Hope traffic hits multi-year high as Red Sea diversions continue
body: Vessel tracking data shows tanker traffic around the Cape of Good Hope has reached its highest level in years, as owners continue to avoid the Red Sea corridor amid ongoing security concerns.

headline: Russia's ESPO blend exports to Asia remain stable despite Western sanctions pressure
body: Loadings of Russia's ESPO crude blend from Kozmino remained steady this month, with Chinese and Indian buyers continuing to absorb volumes at a discount despite ongoing Western sanctions efforts.

headline: US Navy increases presence in Persian Gulf following Iranian naval drills
body: The US Fifth Fleet has moved additional assets into the Persian Gulf after Iran conducted large-scale naval exercises near the Strait of Hormuz, raising concerns of miscalculation between the two sides.

headline: US Gulf Coast crude exports to India tick up as buyers diversify away from Gulf risk
body: US Gulf Coast crude shipments bound for Indian refiners rose modestly this month, part of a broader diversification effort by Indian buyers amid heightened Middle East supply risk.

headline: Iranian gunboats briefly intercept tanker near Strait of Hormuz, no damage reported
body: A tanker transiting the Strait of Hormuz was briefly approached and boarded for inspection by Iranian naval vessels before being released, in an incident maritime security firms say reflects growing operational risk in the corridor.

headline: Major shipping line resumes limited Red Sea transits under naval escort
body: One of the world's largest container and tanker operators announced it would resume a limited number of Red Sea transits under coalition naval escort, citing improved but still fragile security conditions.

headline: Brazilian crude exports to India rise slightly on diversification push
body: Petrobras confirmed a modest increase in term crude sales to Indian refiners, part of New Delhi's broader push to diversify import sources away from Gulf-dependent corridors.

headline: Iran's parliament passes bill authorizing government to close Strait of Hormuz if sanctions escalate further
body: Iran's parliament approved legislation granting the government authority to close the Strait of Hormuz to shipping if the US imposes further sanctions, though implementation would require sign-off from the Supreme National Security Council.

headline: Iraq's Basra oil exports hit record high despite regional tensions
body: Iraq's state oil marketer SOMO reported record crude export volumes from the Basra terminals this month, with buyers including India continuing to lift cargoes without disruption.

headline: UAE's Fujairah terminal reports normal operations amid regional tension
body: The Fujairah oil terminal, a key alternative loading point outside the Strait of Hormuz chokepoint for some UAE exports, continues to operate normally, offering a partial buffer against Hormuz-specific disruption.

headline: India's oil minister says government monitoring Gulf situation closely
body: India's petroleum ministry said it is closely tracking developments in the Strait of Hormuz and has held preliminary talks with refiners on contingency sourcing plans.

headline: Oil prices climb on Hormuz closure fears, Brent nears multi-month high
body: Crude benchmark prices rose for a third consecutive session as traders priced in growing odds of a partial Strait of Hormuz disruption following the latest escalation in US-Iran rhetoric.

headline: Yemen's Houthi movement warns of expanded targeting list for Red Sea shipping
body: Houthi military spokesman announced an expanded list of vessel types considered legitimate targets in the Red Sea, raising concern among shipping insurers and further discouraging Suez Canal transits.

headline: Chinese refiners increase term contracts with Russian Pacific ports
body: Independent Chinese refiners have expanded term purchase agreements for ESPO blend crude loaded from Russia's Pacific coast terminals, tightening available spot volumes for other Asian buyers including India.

headline: Kuwait reaffirms commitment to steady oil supply amid regional tensions
body: Kuwait's oil ministry issued a statement reaffirming its commitment to maintaining steady crude export volumes to Asian buyers regardless of regional security developments.

headline: Tanker rates for Middle East Gulf to India route jump on war-risk premium
body: Very large crude carrier rates on the Middle East Gulf to India route have risen sharply this week, driven largely by escalating war-risk insurance costs tied to the Strait of Hormuz standoff.

headline: Iran conducts additional naval exercises near Strait of Hormuz
body: Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps navy conducted a second round of exercises in the Strait of Hormuz this week, involving fast attack craft and anti-ship missile drills, according to state media.

headline: India's strategic reserves fill rate steady as ministry reviews drawdown options
body: India's Strategic Petroleum Reserve remains near full capacity, with officials reportedly reviewing drawdown scenarios in case of a prolonged Gulf supply disruption.

headline: Panama-flagged tanker changes destination mid-voyage to avoid Red Sea
body: A crude tanker bound for the Mediterranean altered its route mid-voyage to avoid Red Sea transit, opting instead for the longer Cape of Good Hope passage, according to ship-tracking data.

headline: US officials say military options remain 'on the table' if Hormuz threatened
body: A senior US defense official said all military options remain available to ensure freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz, following Iran's latest legislative threat to close the corridor.

headline: Japan and South Korea explore joint strategic reserve coordination amid Gulf risk
body: Japanese and South Korean energy officials held talks on coordinating strategic petroleum reserve policy in response to shared exposure to a potential Strait of Hormuz disruption.

headline: Nigeria's Bonny Light crude sees renewed Asian buyer interest
body: Nigerian crude grades including Bonny Light have seen a modest uptick in inquiries from Asian buyers, traders say, as refiners diversify sourcing away from Gulf-dependent corridors.

headline: Strait of Hormuz transit volumes largely unchanged despite tensions, tracking data shows
body: Ship-tracking data shows crude tanker transit volumes through the Strait of Hormuz remain largely in line with historical averages so far, even as geopolitical rhetoric has escalated in recent weeks.
